theorem_title: Local unmixedness: if $A$ has a regular sequence in $\mathfrak{m}$ of length $\ge \dim A$ and $ps \subseteq \mathfrak{m}$ is weakly regular, every associated prime of $A/(ps)$ has height $\le |ps|$
formal_statement:
namespace DiazModulus

theorem height_le_length_of_mem_associatedPrimes {A : Type*} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    (zs : List A) (hz : RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular A zs) (hzm : ∀ z ∈ zs, z ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A)
    (hdim : ringKrullDim A ≤ zs.length)
    (ps : List A) (hps : RingTheory.Sequence.IsWeaklyRegular A ps) (hpm : ∀ p ∈ ps, p ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A)
    (𝔭 : Ideal A) (h𝔭 : 𝔭 ∈ associatedPrimes A (A ⧸ Ideal.ofList ps)) :
    𝔭.height ≤ ps.length := by
  sorry

end DiazModulus
natural_language_statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m}$, and assume that $A$ has an $A$-regular sequence $zs$ of elements of $\mathfrak{m}$ with $\dim A \le |zs|$ (so $A$ is Cohen–Macaulay). Let $ps$ be a weakly $A$-regular sequence of elements of $\mathfrak{m}$. Then every associated prime $\mathfrak{p}$ of the $A$-module $A/(ps)$ has height at most $|ps|$. A list $r_1, \dots, r_n$ of elements of $A$ is weakly $A$-regular when each $r_i$ is a nonzerodivisor on $A/(r_1, \dots, r_{i-1})A$ (Mathlib's `IsWeaklyRegular`; the last quotient may be zero), and $A$-regular (`IsRegular`) when moreover $A/(r_1, \dots, r_n)A \ne 0$. For a list $ps$, $(ps)$ is the ideal generated by its entries and $|ps|$ its length. Krull dimensions take values in $\{-\infty\} \cup \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$ and heights of prime ideals in $\mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$.

**Proof.** $A/(ps)$ is nonzero, since it has an associated prime. `DiazModulus.exists_isRegular_quotient_ofList`, with $M = A$, gives an $A/(ps)$-regular sequence $ts$ in $\mathfrak{m}$ with $|zs| \le |ts| + |ps|$, and `DiazModulus.length_le_ringKrullDim_quotient_of_mem_associatedPrimes` gives $|ts| \le \dim A/\mathfrak{p}$. In any commutative ring, $\operatorname{ht} \mathfrak{p} + \dim A/\mathfrak{p} \le \dim A$: in the prime spectrum the height of $\mathfrak{p}$ is its order height, $\dim A/\mathfrak{p}$ its coheight, and the Krull dimension is the supremum of height plus coheight. Since $\dim A \le |zs|$, all these numbers are finite, and $\operatorname{ht} \mathfrak{p} \le |zs| - \dim A/\mathfrak{p} \le |zs| - |ts| \le |ps|$.

**Novelty.** Classical; routine formalisation.
source: The local form of Macaulay's unmixedness theorem: W. Bruns and J. Herzog, Cohen–Macaulay Rings, Cambridge Studies in Advanced Mathematics 39, Cambridge University Press, Th. 2.1.6 (the unmixedness theorem) and Th. 2.1.2; H. Matsumura, Commutative Ring Theory, Cambridge Studies in Advanced Mathematics 8, Cambridge University Press, §17. Uses DiazModulus.length_le_ringKrullDim_quotient_of_mem_associatedPrimes and DiazModulus.exists_isRegular_quotient_ofList. C1.2 of the Diaz modulus mission.
